content.title: Props: Data Flows Down
content.hook: A reusable product card should not hard-code every product.
goals: Pass data into child components with props and understand one-way data flow from parent to child.

content.question:
What heading appears?

```jsx
<ProductCard name="Forge Notebook" price="$8" />
```

feedback.correct: The parent supplies a `name` prop, and the child reads it.
feedback.incorrect: The parent supplies a `name` prop, and the child reads it.

content.title: Pass a different value
content.text:
Change this:

```jsx
<ProductCard name="Forge Mug" price="$12" />
```

to show:

```text
Forge Keyboard — $90
```

**Expected:**

```jsx
<ProductCard name="Forge Keyboard" price="$90" />
```

content.title: One-way data flow
content.text:
The basic direction is:

```text
Parent
  ↓ props
Child
```

The child receives the value. It does not rewrite the parent's prop directly.

This makes the path of data easier to inspect.

content.question:
A learner says:

> “I will change the parent’s product name by assigning a new value directly to the child’s `name` prop.”

What is the better model?

options.text: Props are inputs received by the child; the parent controls what it passes.
Every child automatically owns every prop.

feedback.correct: Props communicate from parent to child. They are inputs, not a permission for the child to mutate the parent.
feedback.incorrect: Props communicate from parent to child. They are inputs, not a permission for the child to mutate the parent.

activities.title: Props can be values and functions

content.title: Props can be values and functions

options.text: Props are private memory stored inside a child.
Props are inputs a parent can pass to a child.

feedback.correct: Props carry data and behavior inputs down the component tree.
feedback.incorrect: Props carry data and behavior inputs down the component tree.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Props make data flow explicit from parent to child.
**Senior habit:** When debugging a React component, trace a wrong value upward through its props instead of guessing inside the child first.
nextSteps: Build a child component that changes its displayed output when the parent passes different props.

requirements: Screen-reader accessible code blocks and options
